material_id:
Hari kedua: kita belajar membuat **sopir dan mesin cocok**. Sopir tunggal memakai mesin tunggal, sopir jamak memakai mesin jamak. Di Listening kita kenalan dengan idiom, dan di Reading kita latihan mencari detail dengan cepat.

=== listening
## Idiom: jangan diartikan kata per kata
Idiom adalah ungkapan yang artinya tidak sama dengan arti kata-katanya. *It went over my head* bukan **lewat di atas kepala**, tetapi **saya tidak paham**. Penyusun tes suka memasang pilihan yang memakai **arti harfiah** sebagai jebakan.
Perumpamaan: idiom itu seperti kode rahasia antar teman. Orang luar mendengar kata-katanya, tapi hanya yang tahu kodenya yang paham maksudnya.
> Idiom di kalimat orang kedua → cari pilihan dengan arti kiasan, bukan harfiah
✓ *a piece of cake* = sangat mudah
✓ *hit the books* = belajar keras
✓ *under the weather* = sedang kurang sehat
✕ *a piece of cake* = **makan kue**
✕ *it slipped my mind* = **terpeleset**

=== structure
## Sopir tunggal, mesin tunggal
[[subject-verb agreement|subject-verb-agreement]] berarti [[subject]] tunggal memakai [[verb]] tunggal (biasanya ber-s di present: *is, has, shows*), subject jamak memakai verb jamak (*are, have, show*). Tiga jebakan favorit tes: frasa *of* di tengah, kata *each/every*, dan *there is/are*.
Perumpamaan: frasa *of …* itu penumpang. Seramai apa pun penumpangnya, yang menentukan mesin tetap sopirnya.
> Coret frasa of / with / along with → cocokkan verb dengan kata sebelumnya
✓ The list **of names** is on the wall.
✓ Each of the labs **has** its own rules.
✓ There **are** several reasons.
✕ The results of the survey **shows** … (sopirnya *results*, jamak)
✕ There **is** many exhibits … (yang dihitung *exhibits*, jamak)

=== reading
## Detail: scanning kata kunci
Soal detail menanyakan informasi yang **tertulis** di teks. Ambil kata kunci dari soal (nama, angka, istilah), cari di teks, lalu baca kalimat di sekitarnya. Jawaban benar biasanya memakai parafrase, bukan kata yang persis sama.
Perumpamaan: scanning itu seperti mencari nama temanmu di daftar wisuda. Kamu tidak membaca semua nama, matamu melompat ke huruf depannya.
> Kata kunci soal → temukan di teks → baca 1 kalimat → cocokkan parafrase
✓ Pakai kata yang jarang (nama, angka, istilah) sebagai kata kunci
✓ Baca satu kalimat sebelum dan sesudahnya bila perlu
✓ Untuk soal *According to paragraph 3*, langsung ke paragraf 3
✕ Memilih jawaban karena **terdengar benar** padahal tidak tertulis
✕ Membaca ulang seluruh teks untuk setiap soal
material_en:
Day two: we learn to make the **driver and engine match**. A singular driver takes a singular engine; a plural driver takes a plural engine. In Listening we meet idioms, and in Reading we practise finding details fast.

=== listening
## Idioms: never translate word by word
An idiom is a phrase whose meaning differs from its words. *It went over my head* doesn't mean something flew above someone; it means **I didn't understand**. Test writers love options that use the **literal meaning** as a trap.
Analogy: an idiom is a secret code between friends. Outsiders hear the words, but only people who know the code get the message.
> Idiom in the second speaker's line → choose the figurative meaning, not the literal one
✓ *a piece of cake* = very easy
✓ *hit the books* = study hard
✓ *under the weather* = feeling ill
✕ *a piece of cake* = **eating cake**
✕ *it slipped my mind* = **someone slipped**

=== structure
## Singular driver, singular engine
[[subject-verb agreement|subject-verb-agreement]] means a singular [[subject]] takes a singular [[verb]] (usually with -s in the present: *is, has, shows*) and a plural subject takes a plural verb (*are, have, show*). Three favourite test traps: an *of*-phrase in the middle, *each/every*, and *there is/are*.
Analogy: the *of …* phrase is the passengers. However many there are, the driver decides the engine.
> Cross out of / with / along with phrases → match the verb to the word before them
✓ The list **of names** is on the wall.
✓ Each of the labs **has** its own rules.
✓ There **are** several reasons.
✕ The results of the survey **shows** … (the driver is *results*, plural)
✕ There **is** many exhibits … (what's counted is *exhibits*, plural)

=== reading
## Details: scan for keywords
Detail questions ask for information that is **written** in the passage. Take a keyword from the question (a name, number, or term), find it, and read the sentence around it. The correct answer usually paraphrases rather than copies.
Analogy: scanning is like finding a friend's name on a graduation list. You don't read every name; your eyes jump to the right letter.
> Keyword → find it → read one sentence → match the paraphrase
✓ Use rare words (names, numbers, terms) as keywords
✓ Read one sentence before and after if needed
✓ For *According to paragraph 3*, go straight to paragraph 3
✕ Choosing an answer because it **sounds right** but isn't written
✕ Rereading the whole passage for every question

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Did you understand the professor's explanation of the formula?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: Not really. It went right over my head.

questions.prompt: What does the man mean?
options: He did not understand the explanation.
The formula was easy for him.
questions.key_sentence: It went right over my head.
questions.key_translation_id: Itu sama sekali tidak masuk ke kepala saya (saya tidak paham).
questions.why_correct_id: Jawabannya ada di kalimat si pria, orang kedua. **It went right over my head** itu idiom yang artinya aku sama sekali nggak paham. **Not really** di awal juga jawaban nggak buat pertanyaan kamu paham nggak.
questions.why_correct_en: The answer is in the man's line. **It went right over my head** is an idiom for I didn't get it at all. **Not really** also answers no to did you understand.

why_wrong_id.1: Volume suara profesor nggak disebut. Opsi ini cuma make arti harfiah **over my head**, suara di atas kepala.
why_wrong_id.2: Catatan sama sekali nggak diomongin.
why_wrong_id.3: Kebalikannya. Dia justru nggak paham. Kata **formula** dipakai sebagai jebakan kata yang sama.

why_wrong_en.1: The professor's volume isn't mentioned. This plays on the literal **over my head**.
why_wrong_en.2: Notes never come up.
why_wrong_en.3: The opposite. He didn't understand. **Formula** is a same-word trap.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak bola yang dilempar ketinggian. Lewat di atas kepala dan nggak ketangkep.
questions.analogy_en: Like a ball thrown too high. It sails over your head and you can't catch it.
questions.tip_id: Jawaban Part A biasanya di kalimat orang kedua. Terjemahin idiomnya, bukan kata per kata.
questions.tip_en: Part A answers usually sit in the second line. Translate the idiom, not the words.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: How was the chemistry quiz this morning? I heard it was tough.

script.speaker: W2
script.text: Actually, it was a piece of cake. I finished in fifteen minutes.

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about the quiz?
options: It was harder than she expected.
She had cake after she finished it.
It was very easy for her.
It lasted more than fifteen minutes.
questions.key_sentence: Actually, it was a piece of cake.
questions.why_correct_id: **Actually** nandain dia ngebantah anggapan si pria kalau kuisnya susah. **A piece of cake** itu idiom buat gampang banget. Kelar dalam lima belas menit nguatin kalau kuisnya gampang.
questions.why_correct_en: **Actually** shows she's correcting his idea that the quiz was tough. **A piece of cake** is an idiom for very easy. Finishing in fifteen minutes backs that up.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikan dari maksudnya. Yang ngira kuisnya susah itu si pria, bukan si wanita.
why_wrong_id.1: Ini arti harfiah **piece of cake**. Nggak ada yang makan kue.
why_wrong_id.3: Dia kelar DALAM lima belas menit, bukan lebih lama.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite. The man thought it was tough, not her.
why_wrong_en.1: That's the literal **piece of cake**. Nobody eats cake.
why_wrong_en.3: She finished IN fifteen minutes, not longer.

questions.analogy_id: **A piece of cake** itu kayak sepotong kue. Sekali hap langsung habis, tanpa usaha.
questions.analogy_en: **A piece of cake** is a slice of cake. Gone in one bite, no effort.
questions.tip_id: **Actually** di awal kalimat kedua sering artinya kenyataannya beda dari yang kamu kira.
questions.tip_en: **Actually** at the start of the second line often means the truth is different from what you think.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Are you coming to the beach with us this weekend?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: I'd love to, but I really need to hit the books before my midterm.

questions.prompt: What will the man probably do this weekend?
options: Go to the beach with his friends.
Help the woman with her midterm.
questions.key_sentence: I'd love to, but I really need to hit the books before my midterm.
questions.key_translation_id: Aku mau sekali, tapi aku benar-benar harus belajar keras sebelum UTS.
questions.why_correct_id: **I'd love to, but…** itu penolakan halus, jadi dia nggak ikut ke pantai. **Hit the books** itu idiom buat belajar keras. **Before my midterm** nunjukin dia belajar buat UTS.
questions.why_correct_en: **I'd love to, but…** is a polite no, so he won't go to the beach. **Hit the books** is an idiom for study hard. **Before my midterm** shows it's for an exam.

why_wrong_id.0: **I'd love to, but…** justru artinya dia nolak ajakan itu.
why_wrong_id.2: Ini arti harfiah **books**. Dia nggak beli buku, tapi belajar.
why_wrong_id.3: Ujiannya punya si pria sendiri, **my midterm**, bukan punya si wanita.

why_wrong_en.0: **I'd love to, but…** means he's declining.
why_wrong_en.2: That's the literal **books**. He isn't buying books, he's studying.
why_wrong_en.3: The midterm is his own, **my midterm**, not hers.

questions.analogy_id: **Hit the books** itu kayak nyerbu tumpukan buku dengan semangat sampai kebaca semua.
questions.analogy_en: **Hit the books** is like charging at a pile of books until you've read them all.
questions.tip_id: **I'd love to, but…** hampir selalu artinya NGGAK. Fokus ke alasan setelah **but**.
questions.tip_en: **I'd love to, but…** almost always means NO. Focus on the reason after **but**.

script.speaker: M2
script.text: You look tired. Are you still going to the lab tonight?

script.speaker: W1
script.text: I don't think so. I've been feeling a bit under the weather since yesterday.

questions.prompt: What does the woman mean?
options: She is worried about tonight's weather.
She has been in the lab since yesterday.
She will go to the lab later than usual.
She has not been feeling well.
questions.key_sentence: I've been feeling a bit under the weather since yesterday.
questions.key_translation_id: Sejak kemarin aku merasa agak kurang enak badan.
questions.why_correct_id: **I don't think so** artinya dia nggak bakal ke lab. **Under the weather** itu idiom buat kurang sehat. Jadi dia lagi nggak enak badan.
questions.why_correct_en: **I don't think so** means she won't go to the lab. **Under the weather** is an idiom for feeling ill. So she hasn't been well.

why_wrong_id.0: Ini arti harfiah **weather**, cuaca. Dia nggak ngomongin cuaca.
why_wrong_id.1: **Since yesterday** nerangin sejak kapan dia sakit, bukan sejak kapan di lab.
why_wrong_id.2: Dia malah nggak ke lab sama sekali malam ini, **I don't think so**.

why_wrong_en.0: That's the literal **weather**. She isn't talking about the weather.
why_wrong_en.1: **Since yesterday** says how long she's been ill, not how long she's been in the lab.
why_wrong_en.2: She isn't going tonight at all, **I don't think so**.

questions.analogy_id: **Under the weather** itu kayak berdiri di bawah awan mendung. Badan rasanya berat dan lemes.
questions.analogy_en: **Under the weather** is standing under a grey cloud. You feel heavy and low.
questions.tip_id: Ada idiom, terus opsinya nyebut cuaca, buku, atau kue? Biasanya itu jebakan arti harfiah.
questions.tip_en: With an idiom around, options about weather, books, or cake are usually literal traps.

script.speaker: W2
script.text: We've been working on these slides for five hours.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: You're right. Let's call it a day and finish them tomorrow.

questions.prompt: What does the man suggest?
questions.key_sentence: Let's call it a day and finish them tomorrow.
questions.key_translation_id: Ayo kita sudahi dulu hari ini dan selesaikan besok.
questions.why_correct_id: **Let's…** nandain saran. **Call it a day** itu idiom buat udahan kerja buat hari ini. **Finish them tomorrow** nguatin kalau kerjaannya dihentiin sekarang.
questions.why_correct_en: **Let's…** signals a suggestion. **Call it a day** is an idiom for stop working for today. **Finish them tomorrow** confirms they stop now.

why_wrong_id.1: Kebalikannya. **Call it a day** artinya berhenti, bukan kerja seharian. Jebakan di kata **day**.
why_wrong_id.2: Ini arti harfiah **call**, nelepon. Nggak ada yang ditelepon.
why_wrong_id.3: Dia justru nyaranin kelarin BESOK, bukan malam ini.

why_wrong_en.1: The opposite. **Call it a day** means stop, not work all day. A trap on **day**.
why_wrong_en.2: That's the literal **call**. Nobody gets phoned.
why_wrong_en.3: He suggests finishing TOMORROW, not tonight.

questions.analogy_id: **Call it a day** itu kayak wasit niup peluit panjang. Pertandingan hari ini selesai.
questions.analogy_en: **Call it a day** is the referee's final whistle. Today's game is over.
questions.tip_id: Soal saran? Cari **Let's**, **Why don't we**, atau **How about**, terus terjemahin idiom sesudahnya.
questions.tip_en: Suggestion question? Find **Let's**, **Why don't we**, or **How about**, then translate the idiom after it.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: Did you buy the new graphing calculator for statistics class?

script.speaker: W2
script.text: Not yet. The one in the campus store costs an arm and a leg.

questions.prompt: What does the woman imply?
options: The calculator is too heavy to carry.
She hurt herself in the campus store.
The store has sold all its calculators.
questions.key_sentence: The one in the campus store costs an arm and a leg.
questions.key_translation_id: Yang dijual di toko kampus harganya mahal sekali.
questions.why_correct_id: **Not yet** artinya dia belum beli. **Costs an arm and a leg** itu idiom buat mahal banget. Jadi alasan dia belum beli ya karena harganya kemahalan.
questions.why_correct_en: **Not yet** means she hasn't bought it. **Costs an arm and a leg** is an idiom for very expensive. That's why she hasn't bought it.

why_wrong_id.0: Berat kalkulator sama sekali nggak dibahas.
why_wrong_id.2: Ini arti harfiah **arm and leg**. Nggak ada yang luka.
why_wrong_id.3: Tokonya masih jual kalkulator itu, **the one in the campus store**. Cuma mahal aja.

why_wrong_en.0: The calculator's weight never comes up.
why_wrong_en.2: That's the literal **arm and leg**. Nobody is hurt.
why_wrong_en.3: The store still sells it, **the one in the campus store**. It's just pricey.

questions.analogy_id: **Costs an arm and a leg** itu harga yang bikin kamu ngerasa harus bayar pakai tangan dan kaki sendiri.
questions.analogy_en: **Costs an arm and a leg** is a price so high it feels like paying with your own limbs.
questions.tip_id: Soal **imply** minta alasan tersirat. Kenapa dia belum beli? Idiomnya yang ngasih tahu.
questions.tip_en: An **imply** question wants the hidden reason. Why hasn't she bought it? The idiom tells you.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Do you know why the library closed early today?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: Beats me. It was open until midnight yesterday.

questions.prompt: What does the man mean?
options: Someone beat him in a game.
The library is open until midnight today.
He closed the library early himself.
He has no idea why it closed.
questions.why_correct_id: **Beats me** itu idiom buat aku nggak tahu. Kalimat berikutnya nunjukin dia juga heran, soalnya kemarin perpustakaan buka sampai tengah malam. Jadi dia nggak tahu alasannya.
questions.why_correct_en: **Beats me** is an idiom for I don't know. Next he says it was open until midnight yesterday, so he's puzzled too. He has no idea why.

why_wrong_id.0: Ini arti harfiah **beat**, ngalahin. Nggak ada pertandingan.
why_wrong_id.1: **Until midnight** itu buat KEMARIN, **yesterday**, bukan hari ini.
why_wrong_id.2: Dia aja nggak tahu alasannya, jadi nggak mungkin dia yang nutup.

why_wrong_en.0: That's the literal **beat**. There's no game.
why_wrong_en.1: **Until midnight** was YESTERDAY, not today.
why_wrong_en.2: He doesn't know why, so he can't be the one who closed it.

questions.analogy_id: **Beats me** itu kayak teka-teki yang ngalahin kamu. Kamu nyerah dan bilang aku nggak tahu.
questions.analogy_en: **Beats me** is like a riddle that beats you. You give up and say I don't know.
questions.tip_id: Perhatiin kata waktu kayak **today** dan **yesterday**. Opsi yang nuker waktunya biasanya jebakan.
questions.tip_en: Watch time words like **today** and **yesterday**. Options that swap them are usually traps.

script.speaker: M2
script.text: I have an idea for our group project, but it's a bit unusual.

script.speaker: W2
script.text: I'm all ears. We haven't come up with anything better.

questions.prompt: What does the woman mean?
options: She already has a better plan.
She is eager to hear his idea.
She thinks his idea is too unusual.
questions.why_correct_id: **I'm all ears** itu idiom buat aku dengerin baik-baik. Terus **We haven't come up with anything better** nunjukin dia beneran pengen tahu ide si pria, karena belum ada ide lain.
questions.why_correct_en: **I'm all ears** is an idiom for I'm listening closely. **We haven't come up with anything better** shows she really wants his idea.

why_wrong_id.0: Ini kebalikan dari maksud idiomnya. Dia malah siap dengerin.
why_wrong_id.1: Dia bilang mereka BELUM punya ide yang lebih bagus.
why_wrong_id.3: **Unusual** itu kata si pria. Si wanita nggak nolak idenya. Jebakan kata yang sama.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite of the idiom. She's ready to listen.
why_wrong_en.1: She says they HAVEN'T come up with anything better.
why_wrong_en.3: **Unusual** is the man's word. She doesn't reject it. Same-word trap.

questions.analogy_id: **I'm all ears** itu kayak seluruh badan berubah jadi telinga. Siap nangkep tiap kata.
questions.analogy_en: **I'm all ears** is like your whole body turning into ears, ready to catch every word.
questions.tip_id: Idiom soal anggota badan kayak **all ears**, **over my head**, **arm and a leg** hampir nggak pernah bermakna harfiah.
questions.tip_en: Body-part idioms like **all ears**, **over my head**, **arm and a leg** are almost never literal.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Did you remember to return the projector to the media office?

script.speaker: M1
script.text: Oh no, it completely slipped my mind. I'll take it there right now.

questions.prompt: What does the man mean?
options: He forgot to return the projector.
questions.key_sentence: Oh no, it completely slipped my mind.
questions.why_correct_id: **Oh no** nunjukin dia baru sadar ada yang kelewat. **It slipped my mind** itu idiom buat aku lupa. **I'll take it there right now** nguatin kalau proyektornya belum dibalikin.
questions.why_correct_en: **Oh no** shows he's just realised something. **It slipped my mind** is an idiom for I forgot. **I'll take it there right now** confirms it isn't back yet.

why_wrong_id.0: Ini arti harfiah **slip**, kepeleset. Proyektornya nggak jatuh.
why_wrong_id.1: Kalau udah dibalikin, dia nggak perlu bawa sekarang dong.
why_wrong_id.2: Kantor media nggak disebut tutup. Dia malah mau ke sana sekarang.

why_wrong_en.0: That's the literal **slip**. The projector didn't fall.
why_wrong_en.1: If he'd returned it, he wouldn't need to take it now.
why_wrong_en.2: The office isn't said to be closed. He's heading there now.

questions.analogy_id: **Slipped my mind** itu kayak sabun yang licin. Ingatannya meluncur keluar dari genggaman.
questions.analogy_en: **Slipped my mind** is like slippery soap. The memory slides right out of your grip.
questions.tip_id: **I'll … right now** habis **Oh no** biasanya artinya tugas itu belum dikerjain.
questions.tip_en: **I'll … right now** after **Oh no** usually means the job isn't done yet.

script.speaker: M2
script.text: So we agree that Rina will write the introduction and I'll do the analysis?

script.speaker: W2
script.text: Hold on. I thought I was doing the analysis. I don't think we're on the same page.

questions.prompt: What does the woman imply?
options: She has read the same page of the report.
She wants Rina to do the analysis.
They disagree about how to divide the work.
She is happy with the man's plan.
questions.key_sentence: I don't think we're on the same page.
questions.why_correct_id: **Hold on** nandain keberatan. Dia ngira dia yang ngerjain analisis, padahal si pria juga ngira gitu. **On the same page** artinya sepaham. Jadi **I don't think we're on the same page** berarti mereka belum sepakat soal bagi tugas.
questions.why_correct_en: **Hold on** signals an objection. She thought she was doing the analysis, but so did he. **On the same page** means agreeing, so they haven't agreed on splitting the work.

why_wrong_id.0: Ini arti harfiah **same page**. Nggak ada halaman laporan yang dibaca.
why_wrong_id.1: Rina ngerjain pendahuluan. Yang direbutin itu bagian analisis antara si wanita dan si pria.
why_wrong_id.3: **Hold on** dan **I don't think…** nunjukin dia NGGAK setuju.

why_wrong_en.0: That's the literal **same page**. No report page is being read.
why_wrong_en.1: Rina writes the introduction. The analysis is what the woman and man both claim.
why_wrong_en.3: **Hold on** and **I don't think…** show she does NOT agree.

questions.analogy_id: **On the same page** itu kayak paduan suara yang baca partitur di halaman yang sama. Kalau halamannya beda, lagunya berantakan.
questions.analogy_en: **On the same page** is a choir reading the same page of music. Different pages, and the song falls apart.
questions.tip_id: Soal **imply** plus idiom negatif kayak **I don't think we're…**? Cari opsi soal nggak sepakat.
questions.tip_en: **Imply** plus a negative idiom like **I don't think we're…**? Look for an option about disagreeing.

items.prompt: The list of required textbooks ______ on the course website.
items.why_correct_id: Cari pelaku aslinya: **The list**. Frasa **of required textbooks** cuma keterangan. **List** itu tunggal, jadi kata kerjanya tunggal juga. Daftarnya dipasang orang lain, jadi pakai passive (bentuk di-): **is posted**.
items.why_correct_en: Find the real subject: **The list**. **Of required textbooks** is just a description. **List** is singular, and someone else posts it, so use the passive: **is posted**.

why_wrong_id.0: **are** itu jamak, cocoknya buat **textbooks**. Padahal pelaku aslinya **list**, tunggal.
why_wrong_id.2: **posting** tanpa auxiliary (kata kerja bantu) bukan kata kerja utama. Kalimatnya jadi nggak punya mesin.
why_wrong_id.3: **have posted** itu jamak dan aktif. Seolah-olah daftarnya yang masang sesuatu.

why_wrong_en.0: **are** is plural, matching **textbooks**, but the real subject is **list**, singular.
why_wrong_en.2: **posting** without a helper verb isn't a main verb, so the sentence has no engine.
why_wrong_en.3: **have posted** is plural and active, as if the list were posting something.

items.analogy_id: **of required textbooks** itu penumpang di kursi belakang. Sopirnya tetap satu: **The list**.
items.analogy_en: **of required textbooks** is the passengers in the back. There's still one driver: **The list**.
items.tip_id: Coret frasa **of …**, terus cocokin kata kerjanya sama kata sebelum **of**.
items.tip_en: Cross out the **of …** phrase and match the verb to the word before **of**.

items.prompt: There ______ several reasons why students choose online courses.
items.why_correct_id: Di pola **there is/are**, pelaku aslinya ada SETELAH kata kerja: **several reasons**. **Reasons** itu jamak, jadi pakai **are**.
items.why_correct_en: In **there is/are**, the real subject comes AFTER the verb: **several reasons**. **Reasons** is plural, so it's **are**.

why_wrong_id.0: **is** itu tunggal, padahal yang dihitung **several reasons**, jamak.
why_wrong_id.1: **There has** bukan pola buat nyatakan keberadaan. Yang bener **there is/are**.
why_wrong_id.3: **being** bukan kata kerja utama yang punya tense.

why_wrong_en.0: **is** is singular, but **several reasons** is plural.
why_wrong_en.1: **There has** isn't the pattern for saying something exists. Use **there is/are**.
why_wrong_en.3: **being** isn't a tensed main verb.

items.analogy_id: **There** itu cuma papan petunjuk jalan, bukan sopir. Sopir aslinya duduk di belakang kata kerja.
items.analogy_en: **There** is just a signpost, not the driver. The real driver sits after the verb.
items.tip_id: Pola **there + be**: lirik kata benda setelahnya buat milih **is** atau **are**.
items.tip_en: **There + be**: check the noun after it to pick **is** or **are**.

items.prompt: Every student and teacher ______ to wear an ID card on campus.
items.why_correct_id: **Every** bikin pelakunya dihitung satu-satu, jadi dianggap tunggal walaupun ada **and**. Kata kerjanya tunggal plus passive, karena diwajibkan aturan: **is required**.
items.why_correct_en: **Every** makes the subject count one by one, so it's singular even with **and**. A singular passive verb, required by the rules: **is required**.

why_wrong_id.0: **are** itu jamak. Biasanya **A and B** memang jamak, tapi **every** bikin jadi tunggal.
why_wrong_id.1: **requiring** tanpa auxiliary (kata kerja bantu) bukan kata kerja utama.
why_wrong_id.2: **have required** itu jamak dan aktif. Seolah-olah mahasiswanya yang ngewajibin sesuatu.

why_wrong_en.0: **are** is plural. **A and B** usually is, but **every** makes it singular.
why_wrong_en.1: **requiring** with no helper verb isn't a main verb.
why_wrong_en.2: **have required** is plural and active, as if students were requiring something.

items.analogy_id: **Every** itu kayak petugas absen yang manggil satu-satu. Tiap orang dipanggil sendiri, jadi tunggal.
items.analogy_en: **Every** is a roll call. Each person is called alone, so it's singular.

items.prompt: The number of international students at the university ______ steadily since 2015.
items.why_correct_id: **The number of …** artinya jumlahnya, alias satu angka. Jadi tunggal. **since 2015** butuh present perfect (have/has + V3). Tunggal plus present perfect jadinya **has grown**.
items.why_correct_en: **The number of …** means the total, one figure, so it's singular. **since 2015** calls for the present perfect. Singular plus present perfect gives **has grown**.

why_wrong_id.1: **have** itu jamak. Pas buat **A number of students**, tapi **THE number** itu tunggal.
why_wrong_id.2: **growing** tanpa auxiliary (kata kerja bantu) bukan kata kerja utama.
why_wrong_id.3: **are grown** itu passive (be + V3). Padahal jumlahnya naik sendiri, bukan ditumbuhin.

why_wrong_en.1: **have** is plural. It fits **A number of students**, but **THE number** is singular.
why_wrong_en.2: **growing** with no helper verb isn't a main verb.
why_wrong_en.3: **are grown** is passive, but the number grows by itself.

items.analogy_id: **The number** itu papan skor dengan satu angka. **A number of** itu kerumunan penonton. Papan skornya satu, penontonnya banyak.
items.analogy_en: **The number** is a scoreboard with one figure. **A number of** is a crowd. One scoreboard, many people.
items.tip_id: **THE number of** itu tunggal. **A number of** itu jamak.
items.tip_en: **THE number of** is singular. **A number of** is plural.

items.prompt: The {A}results{/A} of the survey {B}shows{/B} that {C}most{/C} students {D}prefer{/D} morning classes.
items.why_correct_id: Pelaku aslinya **The results**, jamak. **of the survey** cuma keterangan. Pelaku jamak pakai kata kerja tanpa -s, jadi **shows** harus jadi **show**.
items.why_correct_en: The real subject is **The results**, plural. **of the survey** is just a description. Plural subjects drop the -s, so **shows** should be **show**.

why_wrong_id.0: **results** itu jamak, pas jadi pelaku.
why_wrong_id.2: **most students** itu pola yang aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **students** jamak plus **prefer** tanpa -s. Aman.

why_wrong_en.0: **results** is a correct plural subject.
why_wrong_en.2: **most students** is a fine pattern.
why_wrong_en.3: Plural **students** plus **prefer** without -s. Fine.

items.analogy_id: **Survey** itu penumpang yang duduk paling dekat sama mesin, tapi tetap bukan sopir. Sopirnya **results**.
items.analogy_en: **Survey** is the passenger sitting closest to the engine, but it isn't the driver. **Results** is.
items.tip_id: Kata benda pas sebelum kata kerja belum tentu pelakunya. Cek ada **of** di antaranya nggak.
items.tip_en: The noun right before the verb isn't always the subject. Check for an **of** in between.

items.why_correct_id: Pelakunya **Each**, bukan **laboratories**. **Each** selalu tunggal, dan kata **its** yang tunggal juga ngasih petunjuk. Jadi **have** harus jadi **has**.
items.why_correct_en: The subject is **Each**, not **laboratories**. **Each** is always singular, and the singular **its** is a clue too. So **have** should be **has**.

why_wrong_id.0: **Each of the …** itu pola yang aman.
why_wrong_id.2: **safety** dipakai buat nerangin **rules**, aturan keselamatan. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **rules** jamak itu wajar. Satu lab bisa punya banyak aturan.

why_wrong_en.0: **Each of the …** is a fine pattern.
why_wrong_en.2: **safety** describes **rules**, safety rules. Fine.
why_wrong_en.3: Plural **rules** makes sense. One lab can have many rules.

items.analogy_id: **Each** itu kayak kunci kamar hotel. Tiap lab dibuka satu-satu, jadi tunggal.
items.analogy_en: **Each** is a hotel key card. Every lab is opened one at a time, so it's singular.
items.tip_id: Ada **its** di kalimat? Itu tanda pelakunya tunggal.
items.tip_en: See **its** in the sentence? That signals a singular subject.

items.prompt: In the museum {A}downtown{/A}, {B}visitors{/B} learn that there {C}is{/C} many {D}interesting{/D} exhibits.
items.why_correct_id: Habis **there is/are**, yang nentuin kata kerjanya itu kata benda sesudahnya: **many interesting exhibits**, jamak. Jadi **is** harus jadi **are**.
items.why_correct_en: After **there is/are**, the noun that follows decides the verb: **many interesting exhibits**, plural. So **is** should be **are**.

why_wrong_id.0: **downtown** dipakai sebagai keterangan tempat setelah kata benda. Aman.
why_wrong_id.1: **visitors** jamak plus **learn** tanpa -s. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **interesting** itu adjective (kata sifat) yang nerangin **exhibits**. Aman.

why_wrong_en.0: **downtown** works as a place word after the noun. Fine.
why_wrong_en.1: Plural **visitors** plus **learn** without -s. Fine.
why_wrong_en.3: **interesting** is an adjective describing **exhibits**. Fine.

items.analogy_id: **Many** itu tanda kerumunan. Kerumunan nggak muat masuk **is** yang cuma buat satu orang.
items.analogy_en: **Many** signals a crowd, and a crowd can't fit into **is**, which seats only one.
items.tip_id: **there + is + many/several/a lot of …** hampir pasti salah. Harusnya **are**.
items.tip_en: **there + is + many/several/a lot of …** is almost always wrong. It should be **are**.

items.prompt: The professor, along with her assistants, {A}are{/A} {B}preparing{/B} the {C}final{/C} {D}exams{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Pelakunya **The professor**, tunggal. Frasa **along with her assistants** diapit koma dan nggak nambah jumlah pelaku. Jadi **are** harus jadi **is**.
items.why_correct_en: The subject is **The professor**, singular. **along with her assistants**, set off by commas, doesn't add to it. So **are** should be **is**.

why_wrong_id.1: **preparing** (V-ing) setelah **be** ngebentuk continuous (sedang). Aman.
why_wrong_id.2: **final** itu adjective (kata sifat) buat **exams**. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **exams** jamak itu wajar sebagai objek.

why_wrong_en.1: **preparing** after **be** forms the continuous. Fine.
why_wrong_en.2: **final** is an adjective for **exams**. Fine.
why_wrong_en.3: Plural **exams** is a fine object.

items.analogy_id: **Along with** itu kayak pengawal di samping mobil. Ikut jalan, tapi nggak duduk di kursi sopir.
items.analogy_en: **Along with** is bodyguards walking beside the car. They come along but don't drive.
items.tip_id: **along with**, **as well as**, **together with**, **accompanied by** nggak ngubah pelakunya.
items.tip_en: **along with**, **as well as**, **together with**, **accompanied by** don't change the subject.

items.prompt: Economics {A}is{/A} a subject that {B}studies{/B} how people {C}makes{/C} choices about {D}money{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: Di clause (anak kalimat) **how people makes choices**, pelakunya **people**, dan itu selalu jamak. Pelaku jamak pakai kata kerja tanpa -s, jadi **makes** harus jadi **make**.
items.why_correct_en: In **how people makes choices**, the subject is **people**, which is always plural. Plural subjects drop the -s, so **makes** should be **make**.

why_wrong_id.0: Nama bidang studi kayak **Economics** dianggap tunggal walaupun akhirannya -s. Jadi **is** aman.
why_wrong_id.1: **that** nunjuk ke **a subject**, tunggal. Jadi **studies** aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **money** itu uncountable noun (kata benda tak terhitung). Pas tanpa -s.

why_wrong_en.0: Field names like **Economics** are singular despite the -s. **is** is fine.
why_wrong_en.1: **that** refers to **a subject**, singular, so **studies** is fine.
why_wrong_en.3: **money** is uncountable. Fine without -s.

items.analogy_id: Satu kalimat bisa isi beberapa mobil kecil (clause). Tiap mobil punya sopir dan mesin sendiri yang harus cocok.
items.analogy_en: One sentence can hold several small cars, the clauses. Each has its own driver and engine that must match.
items.tip_id: Cek kecocokan pelaku dan kata kerja di SETIAP clause, bukan cuma yang pertama. **people** selalu jamak.
items.tip_en: Check agreement in EVERY clause, not just the first. **people** is always plural.

items.prompt: The {A}students{/A} who live near campus {B}often{/B} walk to class, but the bus from the city {C}center{/C} {D}take{/D} forty minutes.
items.why_correct_id: Habis **but** ada clause (anak kalimat) kedua dengan pelaku **the bus**, tunggal. **from the city center** cuma keterangan. Jadi kata kerjanya harus tunggal: **take** jadi **takes**.
items.why_correct_en: After **but** comes a second clause with the subject **the bus**, singular. **from the city center** is just a description. So **take** should be **takes**.

why_wrong_id.0: **students** jamak plus **walk** tanpa -s. Aman.
why_wrong_id.1: **often** itu adverb (kata keterangan) frekuensi sebelum kata kerja. Aman.
why_wrong_id.2: **city center** itu frasa benda yang aman.

why_wrong_en.0: Plural **students** plus **walk** without -s. Fine.
why_wrong_en.1: **often** is a frequency adverb before the verb. Fine.
why_wrong_en.2: **city center** is a fine noun phrase.

items.analogy_id: Dua mobil digandeng **but**. Mobil pertama disetir banyak orang (**students**), mobil kedua cuma satu (**bus**). Mesinnya harus nyesuaiin sopir masing-masing.
items.analogy_en: Two cars linked by **but**. The first has many drivers (**students**), the second just one (**bus**). Each engine matches its own driver.
items.tip_id: Kalimat panjang pakai **and** atau **but**? Cek kecocokan pelaku dan kata kerja di clause kedua juga.
items.tip_en: Long sentence with **and** or **but**? Check agreement in the second clause too.

items.title: The Long Story of the Pencil
items.body:
The ordinary pencil has a surprisingly long history. Before the sixteenth century, writers in Europe often used thin rods of lead that left faint gray marks on paper. Everything changed when a large deposit of pure graphite was discovered in Borrowdale, England, around 1565. Local shepherds first used the soft black mineral to mark their sheep, but people soon realized that it also made dark, clear lines on paper.

Graphite, however, is brittle and dirties the hands. To solve this problem, early users wrapped the sticks in string or sheepskin. Later, Italian craftsmen placed graphite inside hollowed-out pieces of wood, creating a design very close to the modern pencil.

For more than two hundred years, England controlled the best supply of graphite, and **it** guarded the Borrowdale mine closely. Other countries had to find alternatives. In 1795, a French officer named Nicolas-Jacques Conté developed a method of mixing powdered graphite with clay and baking the mixture in a kiln. This process had two important advantages. It required much less graphite, and by changing the amount of clay, manufacturers could make pencils that were harder or softer.

Conté's method is still used today. The familiar grading system, with labels such as HB or 2B, reflects the **proportion** of clay to graphite. Pencils with more clay are harder and produce lighter lines, while those with more graphite are softer and darker.

In the nineteenth century, factories in Germany and the United States began producing pencils on a massive scale. According to one popular account, yellow paint became common on pencils in the 1890s because manufacturers wanted to suggest that their graphite came from China, where the color was linked to respect and quality. Today, billions of pencils are made every year, and the simple tool remains a favorite of students, artists, and engineers.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did shepherds first use graphite for?
questions.evidence_quote: Local shepherds first used the soft black mineral to mark their sheep
questions.why_correct_id: Kata kunci soalnya **shepherds**. Scanning, ketemu di akhir paragraf 1. Kalimatnya bilang mereka pertama kali pakai mineral hitam itu buat nandain domba mereka.
questions.why_correct_en: The keyword is **shepherds**. Scanning finds it at the end of paragraph 1. They first used the black mineral to mark their sheep.

why_wrong_id.0: Nulis surat nggak disebut. Yang disebut belakangan cuma garis di kertas secara umum.
why_wrong_id.2: Pensil berbungkus kayu dibikin belakangan sama pengrajin Italia, bukan sama gembala.
why_wrong_id.3: Nggak ada cerita gembala jualan ke pengrajin Italia di teks.

why_wrong_en.0: Letters aren't mentioned. The text later mentions lines on paper in general.
why_wrong_en.2: Wooden pencils came later, from Italian craftsmen, not shepherds.
why_wrong_en.3: No sale from shepherds to Italian craftsmen appears in the text.

questions.analogy_id: Kata kunci **shepherds** itu kayak nama unik di daftar hadir. Cuma muncul sekali, jadi gampang ketemu.
questions.analogy_en: **Shepherds** is like a rare name on a register. It shows up once, so it's easy to spot.
questions.tip_id: Pilih kata kunci yang paling jarang muncul buat scanning, kayak **shepherds**, **Conté**, atau **1795**.
questions.tip_en: Scan for the rarest keyword, like **shepherds**, **Conté**, or **1795**.

questions.prompt: The word **it** in paragraph 3 refers to
questions.evidence_quote: England controlled the best supply of graphite, and it guarded the Borrowdale mine closely.
questions.why_correct_id: **it** itu pelaku dari **guarded the Borrowdale mine**, yang jaga tambang. Siapa yang jaga tambang? Yang nguasain pasokan, yaitu England. Coba ganti: **England guarded the Borrowdale mine closely**. Pas.
questions.why_correct_en: **it** is the subject of **guarded the Borrowdale mine**. Who guarded the mine? Whoever controlled the supply: England. Try it: **England guarded the Borrowdale mine closely**. It fits.

why_wrong_id.0: Grafit nggak bisa jagain tambang.
why_wrong_id.1: **supply** itu barang yang dijaga, bukan yang jaga.
why_wrong_id.3: Tambang Borrowdale itu objek yang dijaga. Tambang nggak bisa jagain dirinya sendiri.

why_wrong_en.0: Graphite can't guard a mine.
why_wrong_en.1: The **supply** is what's guarded, not who guards it.
why_wrong_en.3: The mine is what's being guarded. It can't guard itself.

questions.analogy_id: Pronoun (kata ganti) di clause kedua sering nunjuk sopir di clause pertama. Kayak sopir yang sama lanjut jalan habis lampu merah.
questions.analogy_en: A pronoun in a second clause often points to the first clause's driver, like the same driver carrying on after a red light.
questions.tip_id: Ganti pronoun-nya pakai tiap opsi. Pilih yang bikin kalimatnya masuk akal.
questions.tip_en: Swap the pronoun for each option and keep the one that makes sense.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 3, one advantage of Conté's method was that it
questions.why_correct_id: Soalnya nunjuk paragraf 3, jadi langsung ke sana. Cari kata **advantages**. Teks nyebut dua keuntungan, yang pertama **It required much less graphite**, butuh grafit jauh lebih sedikit. **Used less graphite** itu parafrasenya.
questions.why_correct_en: The question points to paragraph 3, so go there. Find **advantages**. The first one is **It required much less graphite**. **Used less graphite** paraphrases it.

why_wrong_id.1: Metode Conté justru NYAMPUR grafit sama tanah liat, **clay**.
why_wrong_id.2: Metode ini dibikin karena negara lain NGGAK bisa pakai tambang Borrowdale.
why_wrong_id.3: Penemunya perwira Prancis bernama Conté, bukan gembala Inggris.

why_wrong_en.1: Conté's method MIXES graphite with **clay**.
why_wrong_en.2: It was created because other countries COULDN'T use the Borrowdale mine.
why_wrong_en.3: It was invented by a French officer, Conté, not English shepherds.

questions.analogy_id: Soal yang nyebut nomor paragraf itu kayak alamat lengkap. Nggak usah keliling kota, langsung ke rumahnya.
questions.analogy_en: A question naming a paragraph is a full address. Skip the city tour and go straight to the house.
questions.tip_id: Ada kata **advantage** di soal? Cari **advantage** atau **benefit** di teks, terus baca daftar sesudahnya.
questions.tip_en: **Advantage** in the question? Find **advantage** or **benefit** in the text and read the list after it.

questions.prompt: The word **proportion** in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
questions.evidence_quote: reflects the proportion of clay to graphite
questions.why_correct_id: Kalimatnya bahas perbandingan tanah liat sama grafit, **of clay to graphite**. Kalimat berikutnya ngejelasin: lebih banyak tanah liat makin keras, lebih banyak grafit makin lunak. Jadi **proportion** artinya perbandingan jumlah: **ratio**.
questions.why_correct_en: The sentence compares clay to graphite, **of clay to graphite**. Next: more clay means harder, more graphite means softer. So **proportion** means a comparison of amounts: **ratio**.

why_wrong_id.0: Warna pensil dibahas di paragraf 5, bukan di sini.
why_wrong_id.1: Harga nggak dibahas di sistem nilai HB/2B.
why_wrong_id.2: Berat nggak disebut. Yang dibandingin jumlah dua bahan.

why_wrong_en.0: Colour comes up in paragraph 5, not here.
why_wrong_en.1: Price isn't part of the HB/2B system.
why_wrong_en.2: Weight isn't mentioned. The amounts of two materials are compared.

questions.analogy_id: Pola **X of A to B** itu kayak resep kopi susu. Perbandingan kopi sama susu yang nentuin rasanya.
questions.analogy_en: **X of A to B** is a coffee recipe. The ratio of coffee to milk decides the taste.
questions.tip_id: Pola **the ___ of A to B** hampir selalu artinya perbandingan, **ratio**.
questions.tip_en: **the ___ of A to B** almost always means a **ratio**.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, a pencil with more clay
questions.evidence_quote: Pencils with more clay are harder and produce lighter lines
questions.why_correct_id: Kata kuncinya **more clay**. Scanning, ketemu di akhir paragraf 4: pensil dengan lebih banyak tanah liat lebih keras dan garisnya lebih terang.
questions.why_correct_en: Keyword: **more clay**. Scanning finds it at the end of paragraph 4. Pencils with more clay are harder and make lighter lines.

why_wrong_id.0: Garis lebih gelap itu hasil pensil yang grafitnya lebih banyak.
why_wrong_id.1: Tanah liat lebih banyak bikin pensil LEBIH KERAS, bukan lebih lunak.
why_wrong_id.3: Gampang patah nggak disebut. Yang disebut rapuh itu grafit murni di paragraf 2.

why_wrong_en.0: Darker lines come from more graphite.
why_wrong_en.1: More clay makes a pencil HARDER, not softer.
why_wrong_en.3: Breaking easily isn't mentioned. Pure graphite is called brittle in paragraph 2.

questions.analogy_id: Kalimat perbandingan **A …, while B …** itu kayak jungkat-jungkit. Satu sisi naik, sisi lain turun. Jangan ketuker sisinya.
questions.analogy_en: **A …, while B …** is a see-saw. One side up, the other down. Don't mix up the sides.
questions.tip_id: Di kalimat **while**, cek baik-baik bagian mana yang ditanya.
questions.tip_en: In a **while** sentence, check carefully which half the question is about.

items.title: How Coral Reefs Grow
items.body:
Coral reefs look like colorful underwater rocks, but they are built by living animals. Each reef is made up of thousands of tiny creatures called polyps, many of which are only a few millimeters across. A polyp has a soft body and a ring of tentacles around its mouth. To protect itself, it produces a hard skeleton of calcium carbonate, the same material found in seashells.

When a polyp dies, its skeleton remains, and new polyps grow on top of it. Over many centuries, these layers of skeletons pile up and form a reef. The process is slow: many reefs grow only about one to three centimeters per year. Some of the largest reefs in the world are therefore thousands of years old.

Most reef-building corals depend on a partnership with microscopic algae that live inside their tissues. The algae use sunlight to produce food through photosynthesis, and they share much of **this** with the coral. In return, the coral gives the algae a safe place to live. The algae also give many corals their bright colors.

Because the algae need sunlight, reef-building corals grow mainly in clear, shallow water, usually less than fifty meters deep. They also require warm water, generally between 23 and 29 degrees Celsius. If the water becomes too hot for several weeks, the coral may expel the algae. Without them, the coral turns white, a condition known as bleaching. A bleached coral is not dead, but it is **vulnerable**; if conditions do not improve, it may starve.

Although reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, they support roughly a quarter of all known marine species. For this reason, scientists often compare them to tropical rainforests.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, coral skeletons are made of
questions.evidence_quote: it produces a hard skeleton of calcium carbonate
questions.why_correct_id: Kata kuncinya **skeleton**. Scanning, ketemu di akhir paragraf 1: polyp ngehasilin rangka keras dari kalsium karbonat.
questions.why_correct_en: Keyword: **skeleton**. Scanning finds it at the end of paragraph 1. The polyp produces a hard skeleton of calcium carbonate.

why_wrong_id.0: Alga hidup DI DALAM jaringan karang, bukan bahan rangkanya.
why_wrong_id.2: Pasir nggak disebut di teks.
why_wrong_id.3: Tentakel itu bagian badan polyp yang lunak, bukan rangka.

why_wrong_en.0: Algae live INSIDE the coral's tissues. They aren't the skeleton.
why_wrong_en.2: Sand isn't mentioned.
why_wrong_en.3: Tentacles are the polyp's soft body, not its skeleton.

questions.analogy_id: Nyari detail itu kayak nyari kunci di tas. Kamu udah tahu bentuknya (**skeleton**), tinggal ngerogoh kantong yang pas.
questions.analogy_en: Finding a detail is like finding keys in a bag. You know what you want (**skeleton**), so reach into the right pocket.
questions.tip_id: Istilah sains di soal biasanya muncul persis di teks. Scanning istilahnya dulu.
questions.tip_en: Science terms in the question usually appear word for word. Scan for the term first.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how fast do many reefs grow?
options: About one to three centimeters per year
questions.evidence_quote: many reefs grow only about one to three centimeters per year
questions.why_correct_id: Soalnya soal kecepatan, jadi cari angka plus satuan waktu. Paragraf 2 bilang banyak terumbu cuma tumbuh sekitar satu sampai tiga senti per tahun.
questions.why_correct_en: It's about speed, so look for a number plus a time unit. Paragraph 2 says many reefs grow only about one to three centimeters per year.

why_wrong_id.1: **Fifty meters** itu batas kedalaman air di paragraf 4, bukan kecepatan tumbuh.
why_wrong_id.2: **23** itu suhu air minimum dalam derajat Celsius, bukan sentimeter.
why_wrong_id.3: **A few millimeters** itu ukuran polyp di paragraf 1, bukan kecepatan per hari.

why_wrong_en.1: **Fifty meters** is the water depth in paragraph 4, not growth speed.
why_wrong_en.2: **23** is a temperature in degrees Celsius, not centimeters.
why_wrong_en.3: **A few millimeters** is a polyp's size in paragraph 1, not daily growth.

questions.analogy_id: Angka di teks itu kayak nomor rumah di satu jalan. Semuanya angka, tapi tiap angka punya pemilik beda. Cocokin angka sama satuannya.
questions.analogy_en: Numbers in a passage are house numbers on one street. All numbers, different owners. Match each number to its unit.
questions.tip_id: Soal angka? Cocokin satuannya: cm per tahun, meter, derajat. Pengecoh sering minjem angka dari kalimat lain.
questions.tip_en: Number questions? Match the unit: cm per year, meters, degrees. Distractors borrow numbers from other sentences.

questions.prompt: The word **this** in paragraph 3 refers to
options: the food made by the algae
questions.evidence_quote: The algae use sunlight to produce food through photosynthesis, and they share much of this with the coral.
questions.why_correct_id: **this** itu objek dari **share much of**, ngebagi sebagian besar. Apa yang dibagi alga ke karang? Makanan hasil fotosintesis. Coba ganti: **they share much of the food with the coral**. Pas.
questions.why_correct_en: **this** is the object of **share much of**. What do the algae share with the coral? The food from photosynthesis. Try it: **they share much of the food with the coral**. It fits.

why_wrong_id.0: Sinar matahari dipakai alga, tapi alga nggak ngebagi sinar matahari ke karang.
why_wrong_id.2: Tempat aman itu pemberian KARANG ke alga di kalimat berikutnya. Arahnya kebalik.
why_wrong_id.3: Jaringan karang itu tempat tinggal alga, bukan sesuatu yang dibagi.

why_wrong_en.0: The algae use sunlight but don't share it with the coral.
why_wrong_en.2: The safe place is what the CORAL gives the algae, in the next sentence. Wrong direction.
why_wrong_en.3: The tissues are where the algae live, not something shared.

questions.analogy_id: Kerja sama alga dan karang itu kayak anak kos. Alga bayar sewa pakai makanan, karang ngasih kamar.
questions.analogy_en: The algae and coral deal is like renting a room. The algae pay rent in food, the coral gives the room.
questions.tip_id: **this** atau **that** biasanya nunjuk ke benda atau gagasan yang baru aja disebut di clause sebelumnya.
questions.tip_en: **this** or **that** usually points to the thing or idea just named in the previous clause.

questions.prompt: The word **vulnerable** in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
questions.evidence_quote: A bleached coral is not dead, but it is vulnerable; if conditions do not improve, it may starve.
questions.why_correct_id: Kata **but** nunjukin kontras: karangnya belum mati, TAPI lagi dalam kondisi tertentu. Kalimat habis titik koma ngejelasin kalau dia bisa kelaparan kalau kondisinya nggak membaik. Jadi **vulnerable** artinya **easily harmed**, rentan.
questions.why_correct_en: **but** shows a contrast: the coral isn't dead, BUT it's in some state. After the semicolon we learn it may starve if things don't improve. So **vulnerable** means **easily harmed**.

why_wrong_id.1: Karang yang memutih justru kehilangan warnanya.
why_wrong_id.2: Teks jelas-jelas bilang **not dead**. Ini jebakan kontras.
why_wrong_id.3: Karang yang kelaparan nggak mungkin tumbuh cepat.

why_wrong_en.1: A bleached coral has lost its colour.
why_wrong_en.2: The text clearly says **not dead**. A contrast trap.
why_wrong_en.3: A starving coral isn't growing quickly.

questions.analogy_id: Rentan itu kayak orang yang baru sembuh dari sakit. Belum parah, tapi gampang kambuh kalau kehujanan.
questions.analogy_en: Vulnerable is like someone just over an illness. Not badly sick, but easily knocked back.
questions.tip_id: Pola **not X, but Y**? Arti Y berlawanan atau ngelemahin X. Pakai petunjuk setelah titik koma.
questions.tip_en: **not X, but Y**? Y contrasts with X. Use the clue after the semicolon.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 4, coral bleaching happens when
options: polyps produce too much calcium carbonate
the water is too deep for sunlight
the coral expels its algae after the water stays too hot
the algae change color to protect the coral
questions.evidence_quote: If the water becomes too hot for several weeks, the coral may expel the algae.
questions.why_correct_id: Kata kunci **bleaching** ada di paragraf 4. Baca DUA kalimat sebelumnya: kalau air kepanasan selama beberapa minggu, karang bisa ngusir alganya. Tanpa alga, karangnya memutih. Gabungin sebabnya (air panas) sama prosesnya (alga diusir).
questions.why_correct_en: **bleaching** is in paragraph 4. Read the TWO sentences before it. If the water stays too hot for weeks, the coral may expel its algae, and without them it turns white. Combine the cause and the process.

why_wrong_id.0: Kalsium karbonat itu bahan rangka di paragraf 1. Nggak ada hubungannya sama bleaching.
why_wrong_id.1: Kedalaman air ngaruh ke tempat karang tumbuh, tapi menurut teks bukan penyebab bleaching.
why_wrong_id.3: Alganya nggak ganti warna. Alganya diusir, makanya karangnya memutih.

why_wrong_en.0: Calcium carbonate is the skeleton from paragraph 1. It has nothing to do with bleaching.
why_wrong_en.1: Depth affects where corals grow, but the text doesn't link it to bleaching.
why_wrong_en.3: The algae don't change colour. They're expelled, so the coral turns white.

questions.analogy_id: Bleaching itu kayak rumah yang penghuninya kabur gara-gara kepanasan. Rumahnya masih berdiri, tapi kosong dan pucat.
questions.analogy_en: Bleaching is a house whose tenants flee the heat. The house still stands, but it's empty and pale.
questions.tip_id: Kata kunci muncul di ujung proses? Baca 1 sampai 2 kalimat SEBELUMNYA buat nemu sebabnya.
questions.tip_en: Keyword at the end of a process? Read 1 or 2 sentences BEFORE it to find the cause.
